title: On Venus it is literally true.
description:
On Venus it is literally true. Venus takes 243 Earth days to turn once on its axis, and only 225 to circle the Sun. Complete a single rotation and you have already outlived a Venus year, with eighteen days to spare.

One rotation of Venus, in Earth days, the slowest spin of any planet in the Solar System. Its whole year is shorter, at 225.

On Venus the Sun rises in the west. Venus spins backwards compared with Earth and nearly every other planet. Sunrise to sunset, if you could see the Sun through the acid cloud, takes about 117 Earth days.

Venus's clouds hid its spin for centuries. Astronomers could time only the cloud tops, which race round in about four days. When radar first reached the surface in 1962, it revealed that the planet beneath barely turns at all.

Sources:
- https://science.nasa.gov/venus/venus-facts/ (NASA Science, Venus Facts, page updated 23 Jun 2026; read in full 26 Aug 2026): states that a day on Venus would be 243 Earth days long, longer even than a Venus year of about 225 Earth days; that because of the planet's extremely slow rotation, sunrise to sunset would take 117 Earth days; that the Sun would rise in the west and set in the east because Venus spins backward compared with Earth; and that Venus's axial tilt is only about three degrees, too little for seasons.
- https://www.aeronomie.be/en/encyclopedia/venus-backwards-rotation-and-orbital-period (Royal Belgian Institute for Space Aeronomy, BIRA-IASB; read in full 26 Aug 2026): gives the precise figures of a sidereal rotation of 243.0185 Earth days and an orbital period of 224.70096 Earth days, so the year is shorter than the sidereal day; states that the rotation is retrograde and was first measured by radar in 1962; that the cloud tops circle the planet in about four days; and that the solar day is 116 and three-quarter Earth days.
